title: Export your video
summary: Export the sequence to an MP4 file from Export mode.

steps.say: Click an empty spot in the Timeline at the bottom right so it has focus.

check.prompt: Is the Timeline panel at the bottom right outlined in blue as the active panel, with clips on it?

hints: The Timeline is the panel with the V1 and A1 track rows. A blue outline shows it is active.
If the Timeline is empty, drag a clip from the Project panel into it first.
steps.why: Premiere sends shortcuts to the panel with focus, so the Timeline must be active.

steps.say: Press Control M to open Export mode.

checks.prompt: Is Export mode showing, with export settings in the middle and a preview on the right?

hints: You can also click Export in the header bar at the top left.
If nothing happens, click the Timeline first so a sequence is selected.
steps.why: Export mode turns your sequence into a video file you can share.

steps.say: Check that Format reads H.264 and Preset reads Match Source, Adaptive High Bitrate.
hints: Click the Format menu and choose H.264 if it shows something else.
Match Source keeps the size and frame rate of your sequence.
steps.why: H.264 makes an MP4 file that plays almost everywhere and uploads well.

steps.say: Click File Name and type a name for your video.

check.prompt: Has the File Name field been changed to a new name?

hints: File Name is near the top of the settings, above Location.
Leave the extension .mp4 at the end.
steps.why: A clear name helps you find the right version later.

steps.say: Click the blue Location text to choose the folder for the file.

check.prompt: Does the Location field show the folder that was chosen?

hints: The blue text is the current folder path. Clicking it opens a folder picker.
Pick a folder you can find later, such as Videos or Desktop.
steps.why: Choosing the folder now saves searching for the file later.

steps.say: Click Export at the bottom right.

check.prompt: Is an export progress window or progress bar showing?

hints: Use the blue Export button in the lower right corner, not the Export tab at the top.
If the button is hidden, make the Premiere window larger.
steps.why: This starts writing the video file.

steps.say: Wait for the progress bar to finish, then open the folder to find your video.

checks.prompt: Has the export progress window closed with no error message showing?

hints: Exporting takes longer for long or high resolution videos.
Open File Explorer and go to the folder you chose in Location.
steps.why: Playing the finished file confirms the export worked before you share it.
